Blocking passes with no geographic key

Source: R/match.R
pf_default_passes.Rd

npmatch's default cascade blocks every pass on state and only opens up to a cross-state token pass at the end. That is right when query and reference are the same establishment; it is wrong here, because a New York foundation routinely funds a California charity and the address the filer types is whatever was on the check — sometimes the grantee's HQ, sometimes a program site, sometimes a lockbox. Every pass below is therefore state-free.

Usage

pf_default_passes(max_ref_freq = 5000, min_pair_idf = 8)

Arguments

max_ref_freq, min_pair_idf

Token-pruning parameters for the loose pass. Defaults follow npmatch's cross-state pass: a lone shared token must occur in no more than ~645 of 1.9M BMF records to justify a pair on its own.

Value

A list of pass specifications for npmatch::np_cascade().

Details

Note that "no blocking" cannot mean a full cross product: 5,000 grants against 1.9M BMF rows is 9.6 billion pairs. What is dropped is geographic blocking. Candidates are still generated by exact name keys and by a shared distinctive name token (IDF-pruned), which is a recall device rather than a geographic constraint — state is used only downstream, as scoring evidence.
